title: 2000 Plus
paragraphs: A pioneering adult science-fiction anthology built around original stories of future technology, space travel, scientific experiments, and the consequences of invention.
Mutual science-fiction anthology created by Sherman H. Dreyer and produced with Robert Weenolsen.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual run (1950-03 to 1952-01) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Sherman H. Dreyer (creator (performer), producer) (performer), Robert Weenolsen (producer), Elliot Jacoby (composer and conductor), Emerson Buckley (conductor and composer), Walt Shaver (sound, performer, and sound-effects artist), and Ken Marvin (announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

The stories often return to science fiction and speculative futures, future technology and technological anxiety, space travel and extraterrestrial exploration, aliens and extraterrestrial contact, robots, machines and automation, and AFRS rebroadcast preservation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Early adult science-fiction radio anthology boom, Fragmentary 2000 Plus survival record, Korean War opening context for A Veteran Comes Home, and Postwar technological and Cold War context.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]], [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], and [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]].
